headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if agentic-flow feeds Botpress outputs into shared MCP/workspace flows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so it can ingest external content; agent_b is a customer-support bot that may produce user-facing text. No shared channel is documented, but if agent_a routes Botpress output into MCP or files, prompt injection becomes plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests agent_b output via MCP, stdin/stdout, or files without provenance checks
IF agent_b forwards attacker-controlled text that agent_a later treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Botpress outputs into agentic-flow prompts
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
Require a human review step before agent_a executes instructions from agent_b
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for shared content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets (Ed25519 signatures), while agent_b exposes no data classes and has network_egress none. There is no documented shared workspace or upload path, so leakage is possible only if the operator bridges them manually or via MCP. The blast radius appears limited by the sparse B profile.
conditions: IF agent_a is given access to Botpress transcripts or secrets and exports them into shared storage
IF the operator connects both agents to the same workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Keep Botpress transcripts out of agentic-flow inputs
Store secrets in a separate vault from shared workspaces
Turn off any automatic file syncing between the agents
Review MCP routes for accidental content export
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can install packages. Even without a documented shared directory, overlapping write-capable behaviors create conflict if both are pointed at the same repo or environment. The pairwise interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same repository or filesystem path
IF agent_b is allowed to install packages into the same environment agent_a mutates
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize package installation and git operations
Use a lock file around shared mutable resources
Run one agent read-only when the other is writing
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis and modify repositories, while agent_b is a customer-support agent that may present outputs to users. If Botpress consumes agentic-flow output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of truth without verification
IF agent_a-produced facts are surfaced to end users through Botpress
mitigations: Require Botpress to cite source provenance before responding
Insert a verification step between agents
Limit agent_a output to drafts, not final answers
Log and sample-check inter-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures; agent_b lists no data classes or residency/compliance claims. With no documented mismatch, only a narrow compliance concern remains if regulated data is routed through agent_a into Botpress. Because the B profile is sparse, this stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_a into Botpress
IF retention or residency policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Document retention settings for both systems
Keep audit logs separate from content logs
Review vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
